FREE Cozy Twisted Ear Warmer - Quick 30 Min

This cozy twisted ear warmer has been my favorite quick make for fall — it's warm, soft, and that twisted knot in the front just makes it feel a little special.

I made this one in cream with mustard and rust, perfect for chilly morning walks and coffee runs. It uses chunky yarn and an 8mm hook, so it comes together in about 30 minutes. Cozy, beginner-friendly, and so wearable.

Skill level Beginner - cozy & quick
Hook 8 mm crochet hook
Yarn Super chunky / bulky

Before you begin

I've been reaching for ear warmers more than beanies this fall — they keep my ears warm but let me still wear my hair up, and they are so quick to make. This twisted one turned out exactly how I wanted — chunky but not too bulky.

What I love about this pattern is the twist. It looks a little fancy but it's actually just a simple fold and seam — no complicated shaping at all. Because we are using super chunky yarn, the stitches grow quickly and the texture really pops.

If you are new to ear warmers, don't worry — we crochet a simple rectangle in half double crochet, then we twist it together in the middle. That's it. One rectangle, one twist, one seam.

Tip from my table: I like to make my rectangle a little snug at first — about 19 inches around. Chunky yarn relaxes after a wear, so a snug fit keeps it from sliding. You can always add a couple chains if you need it bigger.

Materials I used

  • Super chunky yarn: About 70 yards total — I used cream for the main (about 40 yards), mustard and rust for the little color blocks (about 15 yards each). Look for something soft — acrylic or a wool blend both work lovely.
  • 8mm crochet hook: My favorite for chunky ear warmers — it keeps the fabric soft and cozy, not stiff.
  • Tapestry needle: For weaving in ends and seaming the twist.
  • Scissors & stitch marker: Nothing fancy, just to keep track of your first stitch.

Sizing & how to measure

This ear warmer is one size fits most adults — about 20-21 inches around when finished, and 4.5 inches tall. It stretches nicely to fit 20-22 inches.

  • To measure: Wrap a soft tape around your head where you like your ear warmer to sit — right over your ears.
  • My rectangle: I crochet 19 inches long, because the seam and twist take up about half an inch and the stretch does the rest.
  • Width: About 14 rows of hdc gives me 4.5 inches.

Abbreviations

US terms:

  • ch - chain
  • hdc - half double crochet
  • sl st - slip stitch
  • st - stitch
  • BLO - back loop only

Full roadmap - 5 steps

Here is the whole cozy ear warmer at a glance:

Step 1: Chain 40 with 8mm hook (about 19 inches)
Step 2: Row 1-14: hdc across — rectangle 19 x 4.5"
Step 3: Fold & create twisted knot
Step 4: Seam the ends together
Step 5: Weave ends & shape

Step-by-step with photos

1 Foundation chain

With cream yarn and 8mm hook, ch 40. About 19 inches — keep it soft and loose.

2 Body - rectangle

Row 1: hdc in 2nd ch from hook and across (39 hdc). Ch 1, turn.

Row 2-14: hdc across. I used cream, mustard 3 rows, rust 2 rows, back to cream.

3 Create the twisted knot

Fold rectangle in half, make C shape, tuck one side into other, pinch 4 layers together.

4 Seam it together

Sew through all 4 layers in middle with tapestry needle. Pull snug but soft.

5 Finish & shape

Weave ends, shape twist with fingers.

How I finish mine

I weave my ends going back and forth a couple times, then shape with hands. For photos, I place my ear warmer on folded linen with fall leaves and acorns — little fall morning on my table.

Ways to make it your own

  • Color play: Oatmeal, pumpkin, rust, mustard, chocolate — my favorite fall palette.
  • Solid color: Skip color changes for even quicker make.
  • Wider version: Add 2-3 more rows for 5.5 inches tall.

Caring for your ear warmer

Hand wash gently in cool water, lay flat to dry. Fluff knot with fingers after washing.
